title: `createContextualFragment()` external scripts without `async` run async in browsers
body:
### What is the issue with the HTML Standard?

See https://wpt.fyi/results/domparsing/createContextualFragment-external-scripts-in-order.html?sha=dddcfa6758&label=pr_head&q=domparsing%2FcreateContextualFragment-external-scripts-in-order.html from https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/pull/61748

The result in Chromium, Gecko, and WebKit is:

> FAIL message: assert_array_equals: external scripts without async execute in order expected property 1 to be "slow" but got "fast" (expected array ["inline", "slow", "fast"] got ["inline", "fast", "slow"])

The rest of this report is written by Claude:

> I checked Chrome Canary 158, Firefox Nightly 160 and Safari TP with a local server that delays `slow.js` by 1 s. All three run the scripts as async (`inline`, `fast`, `slow`), while `createElement("script")` with `async = false` runs in order. They also return `true` for `script.async` on a `createContextualFragment()` script before it's inserted, so they leave [force async](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#script-force-async) at its default of true.
>
> Per spec, the parser sets force async to false even in the Fragment scripting mode, where it doesn't set the parser document ([in head, `script` start tag](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#scriptTag)):
>
>> If the scripting mode is not Fragment, then set the element's parser document to the Document.
>>
>> Set the element's force async to false.
>
> The reset in [prepare the script element](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#prepare-the-script-element) needs a parser document, so it doesn't apply:
>
>> If parser document is non-null and el does not have an async attribute, then set el's force async to true.
>
> So on insertion, the script isn't parser-inserted and force async is false, which puts it on the [list of scripts that will execute in order as soon as possible](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#script-processing-src-sync). The same applies to `setHTMLUnsafe()` and the other Unsafe methods with `runScripts: true`, and to `innerHTML` and friends when a Trusted Types default policy enables `runScripts`.
>
> Proposed fix: only set force async to false when the parser document is set:
>
>> If the scripting mode is not Fragment, then set the element's parser document to the Document and set its force async to false.
>
> This only affects the Fragment scripting mode. Document parsing, `document.write()`, and Inert parsing are unchanged. The [force async](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#script-force-async) definition ("It is set to false by the HTML parser … on `script` elements they insert") would need a matching tweak.
>
> #12758 always sets the parser document, so there the equivalent change is to drop the "intendedDocument is parser document" condition it adds to the prepare step. That gives:
>
> - Fragment parsing with `runScripts`: the first prepare returns at "not connected" with force async true, so scripts run async once inserted, like `createContextualFragment()`.
> - Streaming into a connected target: prepare continues to the step that sets the parser document back and force async to false, so scripts block the parser, defer, and run in order, like document parsing.
> - Streaming into a disconnected target: like `createContextualFragment()`, since nothing can block a parser there.
>
> The tests in https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/pull/61748 (`createContextualFragment-external-scripts-in-order.html`, and the `runScripts: true` cases in `stream-html-disconnected-target-scripts.html`) would then expect `inline`, `fast`, `slow`.
